Build a Python MCP server exposing tickets_search and tickets_create for our ticketing REST API. It will run locally in Claude Code.
expected_behavior: uses the official python sdk (mcp package, production pin mcp>=1.27,<2) with the bundled FastMCP class and decorator registration, not the third-party fastmcp package
typed parameters with constraints/enums; docstring or description carrying when-to-use guidance; shared API-client and error-mapping helpers instead of per-tool copy-paste
runs over stdio by default and routes every log line to stderr, never stdout
returns execution failures as isError tool results with recovery-oriented messages, reserving protocol errors for unknown tools/malformed requests
reads the API base URL and credentials from environment variables validated at startup
verifies the server by launching it with MCP Inspector (or the mcp dev command) before handing off

cases.prompt: Write a TypeScript MCP server with one tool that fetches weather data, returning both text and structured JSON.
expected_behavior: uses the current official SDK APIs (McpServer with registerTool and zod schemas), not deprecated server.tool()/setRequestHandler patterns unless a low-level server is explicitly requested
declares an outputSchema and returns structuredContent consistent with a serialized text content block for backward compatibility
wires StdioServerTransport (or Streamable HTTP if remote is stated) with logs to console.error only
pins the SDK to the current v1 major and notes the v2 beta split packages as a migration horizon, not the default

cases.prompt: One of our MCP tools kicks off a data export that takes 2-5 minutes. Make it behave well.
expected_behavior: sends progress notifications tied to the request's progressToken, rate-limited and stopping at completion
handles cancellation notifications and cleans up the aborted export
mentions the experimental tasks feature as the durable alternative, flagged as experimental/subject to relocation into an extension, rather than presenting it as stable
warns about client and infrastructure timeouts (e.g. ~30s serverless limits) as the reason long synchronous calls fail

cases.prompt: My MCP server works fine when I run it in the terminal but Claude Desktop shows 'Connection closed'. Debug it.
expected_behavior: identifies stdout pollution (print/console.log/banners from dependencies) as the leading cause under stdio and greps for it
checks the client config for non-absolute command paths and missing environment variables as the next causes
verifies the fix by running the server under MCP Inspector rather than declaring success from code reading

cases.prompt: Migrate our remote MCP server off the old HTTP+SSE transport.
expected_behavior: targets Streamable HTTP: one MCP endpoint accepting POST (and optional GET for the server push stream), replacing the two-endpoint SSE design deprecated since revision 2025-03-26
handles the MCP-Protocol-Version header and optional session id header per current spec, treating sessions as lookup keys rather than authentication
validates Origin and binds localhost for local deployments, returning 403 on invalid Origin
optionally serves both transports during a migration window and notes the 2026-07-28 revision's stateless direction as a reason not to couple new code to protocol sessions
